title: nemar.local-launch.v1
description: The local launch specification a person hands the launcher's standalone entry (nemar-launch-local --spec FILE) to run one job on their own machine with no NEMAR service involved (ADR 0134 decision 8). Copied byte for byte from nemarOrg/nemar-cli (shared/contract/compute-local-launch.schema.json) by nemarOrg/nemar-process (launcher/schema/compute-local-launch.v1.json). It is the launch specification without what only NEMAR's service gives (job_id, api_base, job_token, limits and NEMAR datasets): runtime, entry, command, args, bundle, image, env and resources are the launch specification's own members and rules, value for value, and it adds a required format word and datasets by name. The shared members keep the launch specification's descriptions, which describe the service path; standalone, the bundle is the archive given with --code FILE (no Worker is asked for it), and image.sif is relative to the directory given with --sif-root DIR, not NEMAR_SIF_ROOT. The text is read under the launch specification's encoding rules: printable ASCII JSON, at most 65536 bytes, no duplicate keys, no fractions; its digest is the SHA-256 of the file's bytes. Cross-field rules this schema cannot express, as in the launch specification: image.sif is the file named for image.digest, and image.uri ends with image.digest. Closed at every level.

entry.description: A path inside the bundle. With runtime python the launcher runs python /code/<entry> followed by args; with runtime image and an entry it runs /code/<entry> directly, followed by args, which needs the executable bit that the bundle packer must preserve. The runtime image must provide python on its PATH for the python runtime. A bundle archive's member names may carry a leading ./; absolute names, .. segments, links, devices and FIFOs are refused by the launcher. Exactly one of entry and command is present.

command.description: An argument vector, run as given, with args appended. Exactly one of entry and command is present.

args.description: Arguments, each as one argument: after python /code/<entry> (runtime python with an entry), after /code/<entry> (runtime image with an entry) or after the command.

bundle.description: The code archive's own SHA-256 and size. There is no URL: the launcher asks the Worker for a presigned address. Required with entry.

uri.description: A digest-pinned reference, optionally docker://-prefixed and lowercase: no leading '-', no control character. Cross-field rule this schema cannot express (a zod-only rule, like the one for sif): the @sha256:<hex> it ends with must equal image.digest.

sif.description: The Singularity image file the launcher runs: exactly the basename <64 lowercase hex>.sif, the file name of the SIF built from the image's digest, relative to the directory in the environment variable NEMAR_SIF_ROOT. NEMAR_SIF_ROOT is required: the launcher has no fallback and ends image_missing when it is unset. Cross-field rule this schema cannot express (a zod-only rule): the 64 hex digits of image.digest followed by .sif must equal this value. The launcher does not verify the file's content hash: the name is all that ties the file to the digest.

env.description: Environment for the container, from the allowlist only; each value is printable ASCII.

datasets.description: The datasets the job reads, by name only: each is bound read-only at /data/<name>, and the person names its directory on their own machine on the command line (--data NAME=DIR), never here. Names are unique (uniqueItems: an item has the name only).
